name: Central Sulcus & Motor Hand Omega Area
function: Divides frontal and parietal lobes. Features a distinct inverted 'Omega' shape representing hand motor (precentral) and somatosensory (postcentral) control. Exhibits motor lateralization based on handedness.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Isolated loss of motor control, weakness, or tactile discrimination specifically in the contralateral hand.

disorders: Major/Minor Neurocognitive Disorder Due to Vascular Disease (290.40 / F01.50)
dsm5Mapping.criteria: Focal neurological signs (monoparesis) consistent with vascular lesion along the central sulcus.

name: Calcarine Sulcus (Primary Visual Cortex - V1)
function: Receives initial retinotopic visual inputs from the LGN via optic radiations. Primary gateway for conscious vision.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Loss of vision in the contralateral visual field with macular sparing if PCA collateral flow is intact.

disorders: Neurocognitive Disorder with Lewy Bodies (331.82 / G31.83)
dsm5Mapping.criteria: Recurrent complex visual hallucinations caused by altered occipital/visuoperceptual processing.

name: Ventral Temporal Visual Stream ('What' Pathway)
function: Processes visual signals streaming from V1 down the temporal lobe to recognize complex shapes, objects, places, and faces.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Inability to recognize familiar objects or faces visually despite intact primary visual acuity.

disorders: Major Neurocognitive Disorder Due to Alzheimer's Disease (331.0 / G30.9)
dsm5Mapping.criteria: Progressive impairment in visual agnosia and visuoperceptual domains.

name: Area MT / V5 (Middle Temporal Area)
function: Enriched in direction-selective motion neurons. Specialized for processing visual motion ('building our notion of motion').

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Inability to perceive continuous fluid movement; moving objects appear as freeze-frame snapshots.

dsm5Mapping.criteria: Visuoperceptual disturbance involving loss of spatial-motion tracking.

name: Orbitofrontal Cortex (Phineas Gage Region)
function: Integrates visceral/emotional signals with decision-making, impulse control, social decorum, and risk-reward evaluation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Profound changes in personality, disinhibition, emotional apathy, impulsivity, and poor judgment.

disorders: Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Neurocognitive Disorder (318.1 / F02.80)
dsm5Mapping.criteria: Early behavioral disinhibition, loss of sympathy/empathy, hyperorality, and repetitive/compulsive behaviors.

name: Wernicke's Area
function: Primary language node encoding dimensions of speech comprehension and semantic decoding.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Fluent, grammatical speech lacking meaning ('word salad'); severely impaired auditory comprehension.

disorders: Major Neurocognitive Disorder with Language Impairment (Primary Progressive Aphasia)
dsm5Mapping.criteria: Prominent decline in language comprehension and object naming.

name: Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex (DLPFC)
function: Central node for executive function, working memory, cognitive flexibility, planning, and top-down emotional regulation.

clinicalDeficit.symptoms: Impaired task-switching, poor working memory, inability to plan, and cognitive rigidity.

dsm5Mapping.criteria: Hypoactivity leading to executive dysfunction, concentration difficulties, and unmodulated negative affect.
